title: CREATE FUNCTION (PL/pgSQL)
description: A function packages a calculation under a name you can call from any query, with real parameters and a real return type. Create a function `discounted_price(price NUMERIC, discount_pct NUMERIC) RETURNS NUMERIC` that returns `price` reduced by `discount_pct` percent (e.g. discounted_price(100, 20) should return 80).
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: CREATE FUNCTION, PL/pgSQL
The body goes between two $$ markers and needs BEGIN ... END; inside them - a single RETURN statement computing price * (1 - discount_pct / 100) is enough, then LANGUAGE plpgsql after the closing $$.
CREATE FUNCTION discounted_price(price NUMERIC, discount_pct NUMERIC) RETURNS NUMERIC AS $$ BEGIN RETURN ...; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql - fill in the RETURN expression yourself.
solution: CREATE FUNCTION discounted_price(price NUMERIC, discount_pct NUMERIC) RETURNS NUMERIC AS $$ BEGIN RETURN price * (1 - discount_pct / 100); END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
explanation: PL/pgSQL is Postgres's own procedural language for function bodies - BEGIN/END wraps the executable statements, much like the BEGIN/END of any other procedural language, and RETURN sends a value back the same way it does in Python.
